answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because mesa only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, jade is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
